{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "app/views/embed/best.html.erb",
      "line": 6,
      "severity": "critical",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Invalid ERB syntax '<%- end if %>' causes template compile error",
      "body": "Line 6 contains '<%- end if %>', which is not valid ERB. The 'if' after 'end' is a syntax error; the conditional should be closed with '<%- end %>'. This will cause the view to fail to compile and result in a 500 error whenever the embed/best template is rendered."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb",
      "line": 11,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Unescaped referer in inline JavaScript allows XSS in Discourse origin",
      "body": "The line `parent.postMessage({type: 'discourse-resize', height: document['body'].offsetHeight}, '<%= request.referer %>');` inserts the raw request referer directly into a JavaScript string without escaping. An attacker who controls the embedding page's URL (which is allowed by the embeddable_host check) can include a single quote and arbitrary JavaScript payload that will execute in the context of the Discourse-origin iframe. This is a stored/reflected XSS vulnerability. The referer must be escaped using a JavaScript-safe method such as `j(request.referer)` or `escape_javascript`."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb",
      "line": 36,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "RSS/Atom feed content imported as raw HTML without sanitization",
      "body": "The `poll_feed` method extracts `i.content` from the feed and passes it directly to `TopicEmbed.import`, which stores the post with `cook_method = Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. Since raw HTML posts bypass all rendering and sanitization pipelines, any `<script>` or other malicious markup in the feed will be stored and served to users viewing the topic, leading to stored XSS. The feed content must be sanitized (e.g., with Sanitize or by using the regular markdown cooking path) before import."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/assets/javascripts/embed.js",
      "line": 17,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Substring check for message origin allows attacker-controlled origins",
      "body": "The condition `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` tests whether the message origin contains the discourseUrl as a substring, rather than exact origin equality. An attacker could host a page on an origin such as `https://discourse.example.com.attacker.com` (which contains the legitimate origin as a substring) and send a postMessage to the embedding page. The check would incorrectly accept the message, allowing the attacker to trigger the resize handler and manipulate the iframe height, bypassing the intended origin restriction. The check should compare `e.origin` to the exact origin of `discourseUrl` using `new URL(discourseUrl).origin`."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/models/topic_embed.rb",
      "line": 25,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Race condition in TopicEmbed.import can cause unique constraint violation",
      "body": "The `import` method first checks if a TopicEmbed exists for the URL, then creates a new one inside a transaction. If two processes invoke `import` simultaneously for the same URL, both may see no existing record, both create a new topic and post, and then both attempt to create a TopicEmbed with the same `embed_url`. The second `TopicEmbed.create!` will raise an ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique exception due to the unique index on embed_url, causing the entire transaction (including the newly created topic and post) to be rolled back. The job will fail and the URL will remain unimported. A safer approach is to handle the unique violation gracefully (e.g., rescue and re-fetch) or use a database-level upsert/lock."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/models/topic_embed.rb",
      "line": 48,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "perf",
      "title": "Unbounded open() in import_remote can hang or consume excessive resources",
      "body": "`TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses `open(url).read` without any timeout or size limit. A slow or unresponsive server could cause the job to hang indefinitely, tying up a worker, or a huge page could consume excessive memory. Consider using a library with timeouts and response size limits, or setting timeouts via open-uri options."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Invalid ERB syntax '<%- end if %>' causes template compile error
findings.body: Line 6 contains '<%- end if %>', which is not valid ERB. The 'if' after 'end' is a syntax error; the conditional should be closed with '<%- end %>'. This will cause the view to fail to compile and result in a 500 error whenever the embed/best template is rendered.

findings.title: Unescaped referer in inline JavaScript allows XSS in Discourse origin
findings.body: The line `parent.postMessage({type: 'discourse-resize', height: document['body'].offsetHeight}, '<%= request.referer %>');` inserts the raw request referer directly into a JavaScript string without escaping. An attacker who controls the embedding page's URL (which is allowed by the embeddable_host check) can include a single quote and arbitrary JavaScript payload that will execute in the context of the Discourse-origin iframe. This is a stored/reflected XSS vulnerability. The referer must be escaped using a JavaScript-safe method such as `j(request.referer)` or `escape_javascript`.

findings.title: RSS/Atom feed content imported as raw HTML without sanitization
findings.body: The `poll_feed` method extracts `i.content` from the feed and passes it directly to `TopicEmbed.import`, which stores the post with `cook_method = Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. Since raw HTML posts bypass all rendering and sanitization pipelines, any `<script>` or other malicious markup in the feed will be stored and served to users viewing the topic, leading to stored XSS. The feed content must be sanitized (e.g., with Sanitize or by using the regular markdown cooking path) before import.

findings.title: Substring check for message origin allows attacker-controlled origins
findings.body: The condition `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` tests whether the message origin contains the discourseUrl as a substring, rather than exact origin equality. An attacker could host a page on an origin such as `https://discourse.example.com.attacker.com` (which contains the legitimate origin as a substring) and send a postMessage to the embedding page. The check would incorrectly accept the message, allowing the attacker to trigger the resize handler and manipulate the iframe height, bypassing the intended origin restriction. The check should compare `e.origin` to the exact origin of `discourseUrl` using `new URL(discourseUrl).origin`.

findings.title: Race condition in TopicEmbed.import can cause unique constraint violation
findings.body: The `import` method first checks if a TopicEmbed exists for the URL, then creates a new one inside a transaction. If two processes invoke `import` simultaneously for the same URL, both may see no existing record, both create a new topic and post, and then both attempt to create a TopicEmbed with the same `embed_url`. The second `TopicEmbed.create!` will raise an ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique exception due to the unique index on embed_url, causing the entire transaction (including the newly created topic and post) to be rolled back. The job will fail and the URL will remain unimported. A safer approach is to handle the unique violation gracefully (e.g., rescue and re-fetch) or use a database-level upsert/lock.

findings.title: Unbounded open() in import_remote can hang or consume excessive resources
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses `open(url).read` without any timeout or size limit. A slow or unresponsive server could cause the job to hang indefinitely, tying up a worker, or a huge page could consume excessive memory. Consider using a library with timeouts and response size limits, or setting timeouts via open-uri options.
